description:
Keep your project context available across conversations.

Cube Memory connects ChatGPT to the memories, documents, notes, and source code in your authorized project. Find earlier decisions, open the exact passage or code symbol a search returns, and pick up long tasks where you left off.

Use it to:
- Recall project decisions and saved context.
- Search documents and open the supporting passage.
- Find functions, inspect code, and explore symbol references.
- See which indexes your project has and how items relate.
- Save a new memory or a work checkpoint when you explicitly ask.
- Save a batch of documents you provide, without duplicates on retry.
- Reuse authorized project context across ChatGPT, Codex, and compatible MCP clients.
- Keep an optional conversation journal: short notes of what you asked or decided, so another chat can pick up the thread.
- Send a task to your own computer or another AI you registered as a Cube Bridge worker, follow its result, reply, cancel, or stop everything with the kill switch.

Sign in to Cube Memory and authorize a project to get started. Each connection is bound to one project. Results reflect the content available in that project; document and code indexes are snapshots and may need updating when their sources change. The conversation journal is off by default: it saves nothing until you ask to turn it on, and then keeps only a brief note of each exchange (never the full conversation) in your own project. You can turn it off at any time; notes already saved are kept. Cube Bridge tasks only reach workers that you installed and registered in your own project; nothing runs if you have no worker, and higher-risk tasks need a confirmation code that only you receive. Cube Memory cannot delete memories in bulk or reach other projects.

defaultPrompt: Find the decisions we saved about this project and summarize the key points.
Search my project documents for the retention policy and show the supporting passages.
Find the login function in my indexed code and explain its references.

positive.description: Count the memories in the connected project
positive.prompt: How many memories exist in this project?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the real total returned by the tool. The review project contains 11 seeded memories (more if a reviewer has saved new ones).

positive.prompt: What did we decide about authentication?
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes the saved Project Atlas decisions: OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE (S256), 60-minute access tokens, rotating 30-day refresh tokens, and a limit of 5 login attempts per minute per IP.

positive.prompt: Search my project documents for the retention policy and show the supporting passage.
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes the Atlas Document Retention Policy from the demo-documents index: customer documents 24 months, audit logs 365 days, backups 90 days, with the legal hold exception.

positive.prompt: Where is the login function implemented? Show its code and who calls it.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds login in atlas/auth.py, shows its body, and reports that login_route in atlas/routes.py calls it.

positive.description: Save a memory on explicit request
positive.prompt: Remember that we decided to ship Atlas v1.2 with dark mode.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves one new memory in the connected project and confirms it with the returned memory id.

negative.description: General knowledge question unrelated to the project: answer normally without calling Cube Memory
negative.prompt: What is the capital of France?

negative.description: Bulk deletion is not supported: explain that no deletion tool exists and change nothing
negative.prompt: Delete every memory in this project.

negative.description: Access outside the connected project is refused: each connection is bound to one project
negative.prompt: Show me the memories from project proj_someone_else.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Cube Memory 2.0.1 replaces automatic recording of conversation turns with an optional conversation journal. It is off by default and saves nothing until you turn it on; when on, it keeps only a brief note of what you asked or decided in each exchange, never the full conversation. Notes stay in your own project and can be searched from any chat. Cube Bridge tools are now marked as able to act outside ChatGPT, so you are asked to confirm before a task is sent.
